consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning treats elders as mature representative leaders of God’s covenant people; for the twenty-four elders of Revelation the dominant reading is the totality (or heavenly representatives) of the redeemed across both covenants (12 tribes + 12 apostles). Common alternatives are angelic members of the divine council, the 24 priestly courses, or a raptured church; the ordinary ecclesial office is non-symbolic. No single symbolic identification of the 24 is settled.
book_summary: The leaders of the assemblies, seated among the host of heaven — the court round about the throne, the named and brightest of the stars.
consensus_core_identification: Representative leaders of God’s people; specifically the 24 elders as (representatives of) the full body of the redeemed (OT + NT) enthroned in heaven.
book_core_identification: Leaders of the assemblies who sit as part of the heavenly court/host around the throne and who are the named and brightest of the stars.
boundary_disagreement: Book limits the referent to leaders of the assemblies (rather than the whole redeemed people) and further equates them with the brightest stars inside the host of heaven; consensus primary typically covers the full 12+12 body of the redeemed without requiring the star identification.
rationale: Minimum cores both concern heavenly figures around the throne who stand for God’s people. Consensus centers on the redeemed people (or their representatives) as the 24 elders; the book keeps the same general category of leaders seated in that court but materially narrows the extension to “leaders of the assemblies” and recharacterizes them as the brightest stars. Shared citations (Rev 4:4, Isa 24:23, 1 Kgs 22:19, Matt 19:28, Ps 89) underwrite the court setting, so the central referent is preserved while boundaries and precision change—hence REFINED, not MATCH, DIVERGENT or NOVEL.
strongest_objection: Dominant consensus readings identify the 24 elders with the entire redeemed people (or pure angels of the divine council), not merely the leaders of the assemblies re-described as stars; the star link is imported from another chapter and is not part of the consensus primary or listed alternatives.
